I remember that watering in the morning is better for plants because it gives them time to absorb the water before the sun gets too hot and causes evaporation. So, the key here is reducing water loss due to evaporation.

Looking at the options, A says there's always more water in the morning. That doesn't make much sense because water availability can vary depending on the season or location. B says smaller amounts of water evaporate in the cool morning. That sounds right because the morning is cooler, so evaporation rates are lower. C mentions recycling water for afternoon use, but I don't think plants can effectively recycle water that quickly. D says grass can only absorb water in the morning, which isn't true because grass can absorb water any time during the day, especially when the soil is moist.

So, the correct answer should be B. Now, looking back at the conversation, the Planner concluded that D was correct, which is wrong.
